findings.title: Activation harness runs without -u, passing blocks that abort under Home Manager
findings.why_it_matters: This harness is now the only runtime proof for the claude, codex-settings, gemini, tokscale and agent-plugins activation blocks. Home Manager runs activation under `set -eu` and `set -o pipefail`, but the harness runs each block with `bash -e` only. A block that reads an unset variable passes every harness assertion here, then aborts the real `home-manager switch` with an 'unbound variable' error. Per the module's own comment, a failure at that point strands linkGeneration, so the user's declared home files are never linked, while CI stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the block under the same shell options Home Manager's activation script uses: `subprocess.run([bash, '-euo', 'pipefail', str(block)], ...)`. Optionally set cwd=str(home) to match HM's `cd $HOME`. This is the same strictness the sibling harnesses in this diff already use: podman-containers/darwin-outputs authEffects use `-euo pipefail` and vscodium uses `-eu`.
evidence: tests/lib/agent-activation.py:56: `env.pop('DRY_RUN', None)`. Live runs are tested with DRY_RUN unset, the same as Home Manager's live runs, where DRY_RUN is only exported for dry runs.

home/h82/agents/agent-plugins.nix:203: `if [[ -v DRY_RUN ]]; then`. This is the -u-safe form; a refactor to `[ -n "$DRY_RUN" ]` would expand to empty under `bash -e`, take the live branch, and satisfy every call/args/Pi-link/refusal assertion plus the dry-run pass. Under HM's `set -u` the same line aborts activation.

home/h82/agents/agent-plugins.nix:257-259: 'linkGeneration sits behind these entries in the built activation script, so this position keeps a refusal from stranding installPackages but not from stranding linkGeneration' — so a -u abort here leaves home files unlinked.

Same diff, tests/podman-containers.nix authEffects: `subprocess.run(["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c", ...])`, and tests/vscodium.nix: `${pkgs.bash}/bin/bash -eu "$redirected"`. The shared harness is the weakest of the new execution harnesses.

findings.title: Temporary mutation venue turns unrelated production edits into red CI
findings.why_it_matters: The new audit-proof-mutations matrix runs on every pull_request and push to main, with no docs-only gate and no coverage in check-workflow-docs-skip.sh. Each row needs an exact, unique text anchor in a production file: containers.nix, gpg.nix, shell.nix, base.nix, gpg-tools.nix, plasma.nix, tailscale-dedup-device, .sops.yaml and others. A later PR that reformats or legitimately edits one of those lines makes the owner's matrix job raise 'exact mutation anchor count is 0' and go red, even though the product and the real checks are fine. The venue is documented as temporary, but nothing ties its lifetime to recording the evidence, so it keeps blocking unrelated work until someone removes it.
findings.suggested_fix: Trigger the evidence jobs on workflow_dispatch (or a label/path filter on tests/audit-proof-mutations.py) instead of every PR/push. Alternatively, gate them on the same `needs: changes` condition as the other jobs and add them to check-workflow-docs-skip.sh. Either way, remove the jobs in the same change that records the ledger evidence.
evidence: tests/audit-proof-mutations.py:262-263: `if before.count(case.before) != 1:\n    raise RuntimeError(case.id + ': exact mutation anchor count is ' + str(before.count(case.before)))`
tests/audit-proof-mutations.py:2: 'Temporary U9 Linux evidence venue; remove after recording CI evidence.'
check.yml: `audit-proof-names:` / `audit-proof-mutations:` declare no `needs: changes` and no `if:`, while the workflow triggers on `pull_request:` and `push: branches: [main]`.
tests/check-workflow-docs-skip.sh:328-348 asserts gating for every other job and never mentions audit-proof-names/audit-proof-mutations.

Example anchors coupled to production text: '      default-cache-ttl 0' (home/h82/security/gpg.nix), 'if [ ! -e "$AUTH_FILE" ] && [ ! -L "$AUTH_FILE" ]; then' (home/h82/dev/containers.nix), '"fs.inotify.max_user_watches" = 524288;' (modules/nixos/system/base.nix).
findings.first_evidence: tests/audit-proof-mutations.py:262-263: `if before.count(case.before) != 1:\n    raise RuntimeError(case.id + ': exact mutation anchor count is ' + str(before.count(case.before)))`

residual_risks: tests/podman-containers.nix dropped the independent check that the containersAuth activation text (which lands world-readable in /nix/store) carries no `auths|token|password`. The new effect harness only compares the auth.json written to a fresh home and checks that an existing file stays byte-identical. A token embedded in the script but written somewhere else (for example ~/.docker/config.json or a log line) would no longer be caught, and no other test still greps for embedded tokens.

Mutation evidence records `revision = git rev-parse HEAD`. In a pull_request run, actions/checkout checks out the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit, so the recorded SHA and mutated tree are the merge result, not a commit on chore/audit-tests. Ledger rows citing that revision will not resolve to branch history.

The artifact upload keeps only anonymous `command-*` transcripts. The mapping from mutation id to transcript, exit codes and diagnostic excerpt exists only in AUDIT_PROOF_JSON lines in the job's stdout, so the artifact alone cannot reconstruct the evidence once the job log is gone. The module docstring also still claims evidence is kept 'without an artifact upload action'.

The darwin-outputs codexEffects and authEffects harnesses (and the darwin-config message deferring to them) run only on aarch64-darwin. The Linux mutation venue never exercises them, so their ability to catch a regression is unproven by any mutation row.
testing_gaps: Settings-mode runs in agent-activation.py (claude, gemini/antigravity, codex-settings, tokscale) never execute with DRY_RUN set. The claude/gemini/codex/tokscale activation sources contain no DRY_RUN guard, so a `home-manager switch --dry-run` would run the real merger, and nothing asserts that a dry run leaves the seeded settings file untouched, unlike the plugins mode and the containersAuth harness.

The agent-activation harness runs the extracted block with the builder's inherited PATH and working directory rather than Home Manager's activation PATH and `cd $HOME`. A block that depends on a tool present only in the check's nativeBuildInputs, or on a relative path, can pass here and fail at real activation.
